items.statement: The change package will reduce the weekly group HPCIA share of systemic antimicrobial prescriptions from about 27 percent to 15 percent or less by the end of January 2027 without raising 7-day re-consultation.
items.rationale: Need is high because the guideline is not followed; novelty is low, which suits local improvement; feasibility and parsimony are high because the measure comes from an existing report and the changes use existing meetings and staff.
items.risks: Substitution towards amoxicillin-clavulanate, brief prompt reasons that change nothing, and a fall in use after the free culture period.

items.statement: Free in-house urine culture will raise culture submission before treatment for suspected urinary infection in cats from about 9 percent to 40 percent or more while it is offered.
items.rationale: Culture cost is the commonest recorded reason for not culturing, and most cultured cats grow nothing (claim c4).
items.risks: Needs manual sampling to measure; effect may end when culture is charged again.

items.statement: Monthly clinic feedback alone, without the prescribing prompt, would achieve most of the reduction.
items.rationale: Feedback was followed by a relative fall of 18 percent in one controlled comparison (claim c2).
items.risks: Separating the components would need more cycles and clinics than the group has.

summary: Three hypotheses ranked; h1 selected as the simplest test of the whole change package.
